finding.summary: `CellIndex.bounds()` can return `Infinity`/`-Infinity` coordinates or an inflated extent because it trusts key presence rather than non-empty buckets and assumes rowIndex/colIndex are both populated
finding.evidence: cell-index.ts `bounds()`: guards only `if (this.rowIndex.size === 0) return undefined;` then reduces over `rowIndex.keys()` and separately `colIndex.keys()` starting from `Infinity`/`-Infinity`. If removal leaves empty-set keys behind (a common CellIndex implementation detail), the extent stays at the deleted cell's row/col forever; if `colIndex` is ever empty while `rowIndex` is not, the returned Range contains `Infinity`, which `resolveRange` will propagate into `toSrefs` — an effectively infinite range enumeration.
